messages:
sre-bot: INCIDENT DETECTED: cont-batching path p99 spike in us-west2. Streaming tail latency up to ~4300ms, error rate +1.8% vs baseline. Auto-mitigation did not trigger (threshold miss).
Maya Chen: oncall here — seeing the same. Which pools are affected? any customer-facing alerts?
Noah Patel: chat-streaming and longform-gen show elevated p99 and increased stream stalls. A handful of customer sessions timed out. Pulling logs from contbatch-pool-7.
Devon Liu: quick metric dump: p95 +700ms, p99 +2.1s, median batch_tokens ~600 but 90th/99th batches jump to 3.8k-4.2k tokens. Scheduler fairness (wait_ms) shows tail tasks >1800ms.
Ira Singh: KV cache eviction events around 12:22 UTC correlate with the spike. Paging logs show heavy reads to backing-store during those windows. Suspect mixed sequence-length packing created huge batches that overflow KV working set.
Maya Chen: okay likely chain: mixed-seqlen -> oversized batches -> KV thrash -> paging -> streaming stalls/tail-surge. Need live mitigation: reduce max_batch_tokens, enable preemptive small-batch path, or route streaming to fallback pool.
Noah Patel: immediate actions I can do now: 1) bump contbatch-pool-7 min_replicas +1 in us-west2, 2) push runtime knob max_batch_tokens=1024 as hotfix (was 8192), 3) enable streaming flow-control (backpressure) for longform-gen. Which should we prioritize?
Maya Chen: prioritize hotfix to reduce max_batch_tokens and enable preemptive small-batch scheduling. Also route traffic for critical customers to dedicated pool if possible.
Devon Liu: prepared a quick hotfix patch: 
```yaml
runtime:
  contbatch:
    max_batch_tokens: 1024
    small_batch_preempt: true
```
I can roll to canary on contbatch-pool-7 in 2 mins.
Ira Singh: note: if we reduce max_batch_tokens we may increase per-token cost, but prevents KV eviction. Customer impact tradeoff is acceptable during incident.
Maya Chen: roll canary, watch p99 and KV eviction rate. If canary looks good for 5m, roll to pool. Noah, start routing customers C and D to dedicated-dyn-usw2-1. Add TTL 30m then re-evaluate.
Noah Patel: routing change done for C/D (temporary). ops-bot shows config applied.
ops-bot: CONFIG_UPDATE: routed 2 customers (C,D) -> dedicated-dyn-usw2-1.
Devon Liu: canary applied (contbatch-pool-7/canary). Observability links: https://console/redwood/obs/contbatch-pool-7. Watching p99 now.
Maya Chen: early signal: KV eviction rate dropped 70% on canary nodes, p99 decreased from 4.3s -> 1.2s on canary. Good. Begin progressive rollout to remaining nodes in pool over 10m window.
Ira Singh: keep an eye on long tail for streaming sessions — enable extra logging for any resumed stalls.
Noah Patel: progressive rollout started. Also added temporary scheduling fairness tweak: max_wait_ms capped at 1200 to avoid one job starving others.
Devon Liu: note from scheduler: preemptive small-batch path engaged; mixed-seqlen packing now tops out at 1.0k tokens per batch.
Maya Chen: updating incident channel and customers: "We saw a transient p99 latency spike causing streaming stalls for some sessions in us-west2. We've applied a hotfix to limit batch size and enabled preemptive small-batch scheduling; routing for critical customers temporarily moved to dedicated pool. We're monitoring and will update in 30m."
Noah Patel: customer impact notes: Customer X saw ~12% stream re-buffering and ~7% session reconnects between 12:20-12:30 UTC. CS already notified.
Ira Singh: started a short log capture for affected requests (sample ids) and will create a regression checkpoint for evals team.
Maya Chen: good. After rollout stabilizes, follow-ups: 1) auto-detect mixed-seqlen packing anomalies (alert), 2) add preemptive shedding knob to runtime defaults, 3) create doc on tuning max_batch_tokens vs KV sizing.
Devon Liu: opened a post-incident item: INFRA-8372 "contbatch: adaptive batch cap + scheduler fairness policies". Linking perf graphs.
Noah Patel: handoff to night oncall: I'll stay 15m then handoff. If p99>1.5s again or paging events spike, page eng-sre.
Maya Chen: thanks. Handoff to Noah. Oncall notes: hotfix id: hf/contbatch/2026-03-15/01, rollout status: progressive complete, current p99 in us-west2: ~950ms, KV eviction rate normalized, routed customers C/D to dedicated pool. Keep tracking for 60m.
Noah Patel: acknowledged. I'll be primary for next 60m. If any re-occurrence, escalate to runtime-team and consider temporary traffic shaping at API gateway.
ops-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: state=mitigated -> monitoring.
Maya Chen: closing live mitigation plan in this thread. Will open a postmortem draft tomorrow with timelines + customer impact. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
Ira Singh: saving logs and notes to the incident folder: https://vault/redwood/incidents/1766609876-contbatch-tail-jitter/
Noah Patel: copy — will notify PMs and CS with summary.
sre-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: mitigations stable, no ongoing paging.
